clue.text: Tête-á-tête constitutes a threat to her

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are said to make up, in a new order, the expression defined

explanation.surface: A private chat between two people poses a danger to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitutes' signals that A THREAT TO HER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is an intimate private conversation between two people, which is a frank exchange of feelings.

parts.note: Hal is the familiar short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
in the old sense 'without' means 'except', as 'but' does

explanation.surface: A king called Henry the First goes without fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry I' reads as a king, but it is two pieces; 'without' is used in its old sense of 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas, an example of a food fish.

parts.note: 'like' means 'as', in comparisons
Kew Gardens are the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London

explanation.surface: Gardens can be laid out crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the famous botanic garden in London. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is crooked or not straight, tilted to one side.

indicators.note: a word without its heart keeps only its outside letters, so the middle of Their is dropped

parts.note: old means aged
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Their elderly father, heart gone, is a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to the answer of 22 down, ACTOR; 'heartless' removes the middle of THEIR, leaving TR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is a performer who specialises in tragic roles, a kind of stage player.

clue.text: To some extent, a provident poet

indicators.note: only part of the words that follow is used, so the letters sit within a provident

explanation.surface: A poet who is to some degree thrifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' signals the letters inside 'a provident'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Henry failing to apprehend complex part of book

indicators.note: complex means intricate or mixed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
Henry fails to appear, so his letter drops out of the word apprehend

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry can't grasp a complicated bit of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' drops H from APPREHEND; 'complex' rearranges the APPREND that is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Endpapers are the leaves pasted inside the covers of a bound volume, joining it to its binding.

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: An artist becomes a member of the club.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to clip is to cut
tough means hard

explanation.surface: Chop up a tough fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like one verb, but 'up' turns CLIP into PILC.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, often tinned.

indicators.note: these words say the letters are what one hears when the word is spoken

parts.note: a grill is a restaurant serving ... food

explanation.surface: A rasping noise comes out of a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating sound' looks like a phrase, but 'Grating' is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating or screen of bars, as over a window.

explanation.surface: Something plumed acts at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathered describes something like a winged creature; the idiom also means easily, readily, with no hesitation.

indicators.note: the brother word goes around the one, enclosing it

parts.note: Brer is a dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit

explanation.surface: Around one o'clock, a brother got up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a verb, but it is the flower; BRER is the Southern US form of brother.
explanation.definitionFit: The brier is a wild rose, such as the sweetbrier or dog rose.

explanation.surface: A sportsman at a match in Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A derby is the American name for the round hard felt hat; a player who delivers the ball in cricket is also called this.

indicators.note: crazy suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A madman obsessed with ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges A LUNATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to seamanship, sailors or navigation.

clue.text: Warning of poison has to be listened to

indicators.note: these words say a heard word gives the letters

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: An alert about poison must be heeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to be listened to' tells us TOXIN is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal.

clue.text: Clergyman takes tea without the trimmings

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
something with no trimmings is unadorned

explanation.surface: A priest has his tea served unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a priest attached to an institution such as a regiment or hospital.

clue.text: Substantial reversion accepted by the wronged wife

indicators.note: the turned word is taken inside the other letters
wronged suggests the word the is put wrong, in a new order
reversion means the word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: substantial means ample

explanation.surface: A large legacy is handed to the wife who was treated unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversion' looks like a legal inheritance, but it signals a turnaround; 'wronged' rearranges THE into HTE, which 'accepted by' wraps round the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is a companion and helper, especially a spouse.

clue.text: Strange happenings flower power gives rise to…

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: an anemone is a flower
HP stands for horsepower

explanation.surface: Weird events arise from flower power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives rise to' turns the whole of ANEMONE plus HP upwards; the dots join it to the next clue's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable occurrences or marvels.

parts.note: re means regarding, in connection with
public means open to all

explanation.surface: Continuing the sentence: linked with open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open country' looks like moorland, but 'open' gives PUBLIC and 'country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state or nation governed without a monarch.

indicators.note: the crying word goes around the girl

parts.note: to cry is to show distress
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is upset over a girl's sharp remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' looks like jokes, but it means small gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Crannies are small narrow openings or chinks.

clue.text: Nut to crunch while being eaten

indicators.note: the word for while is swallowed by the chewing word

parts.note: to chew is to crunch with the teeth
as means while

explanation.surface: A nut to crunch as you eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being eaten' says the word for while goes inside the crunching word; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a kidney-shaped edible kernel from a tropical tree.

indicators.note: the call goes around the disturbance

parts.note: a mew is the cry of a cat or gull
ado is fuss or disturbance

explanation.surface: An informer complains about a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' suggests an informer, but here it is a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grassland, often for hay.

explanation.surface: Someone beat a rival over fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst is to defeat; worsted is also a woollen fabric made from twisted yarn.

clue.text: Programme incorporates friend's return by public transport

indicators.note: return means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an ally is a friend, with the s of the possessive
a bus is a form of public transport, set beside the turned word

explanation.surface: A schedule includes a friend's trip home by bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the possessive ALLY'S backwards, so the apostrophe s counts as a letter; 'incorporates' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is an outline of a course of study.

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill, a rising of ground

explanation.surface: Bill is an up-and-coming performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like a reversal in this down clue, but 'a rising' is a hill, TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a stage performer.

clue.text: Brigade's leader given command to march

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an order is a command

explanation.surface: A brigade commander tells the troops to march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' looks like a verb, but it is a frontier, as in the Welsh Marches.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a frontier or boundary territory.

clue.text: Hamlet, for instance, said to be condescending

indicators.note: these words say the letters come from what is heard

parts.note: Hamlet was a prince of Denmark, a Dane

explanation.surface: Hamlet is reckoned to be snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, to stoop to do something.

indicators.note: the fish goes around the river letter

parts.note: a dab is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A dull fish lies near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts DAB around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and lacking colour or interest.

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a sexist is a male chauvinist

explanation.surface: A male chauvinist has not begun to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't started' drops the S from SEXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, to survive.

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about, rearranged

parts.note: the letters of clarinets, with the s

explanation.surface: The way the clarinet is played is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges CLARINETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A larcenist is a thief, someone who commits theft.

clue.text: Excellent support one man gives bats

parts.note: crack means first-rate
a bra is a support garment
I is the Roman numeral one
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: A supportive man gives cricket bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the noun, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is slang for mad, and crackbrained means crazy.
